meta.disclaimer: Educational clinical reference only — not a prescription. Antibiotic prophylaxis for infective endocarditis is suggested ONLY for patients with the highest-risk cardiac conditions undergoing dental procedures that manipulate gingival tissue or the periapical region of teeth, or perforate the oral mucosa. Good oral health and routine dental care matter more than prophylaxis. Verify against the current AHA statement and local guidance before prescribing.
meta.notes: US figures from AHA 2021 (Wilson WR et al., Circulation 2021;143:e963-e978). Single dose given 30-60 minutes before the procedure. Clindamycin is NO LONGER recommended. Cephalosporins must be avoided in patients with a history of anaphylaxis, angioedema, or urticaria to penicillin/ampicillin. UK/NICE differs (routine prophylaxis not recommended) — tagged separately.

recommendation.summary: Prophylaxis is reasonable for highest-risk cardiac patients undergoing invasive dental procedures. Highest-risk = prosthetic heart valve or prosthetic valve-repair material; previous infective endocarditis; cardiac transplant with valvulopathy; specific congenital heart disease (unrepaired cyanotic CHD incl. palliative shunts/conduits; completely repaired defect with prosthetic material/device during first 6 months; repaired CHD with residual defect at/adjacent to a prosthetic patch/device).

rules.rationale: AHA restricts prophylaxis to cardiac conditions with the highest risk of adverse outcome from IE, and only for dental procedures involving manipulation of gingival tissue/periapical region or perforation of oral mucosa.
rules.source_locator: Highest-risk cardiac conditions; qualifying dental procedures.

recommendation.summary: Antibiotic prophylaxis is NOT recommended for patients who are not in the highest-risk cardiac category, regardless of the dental procedure. Emphasise oral hygiene and routine dental care.

rules.rationale: For all cardiac conditions other than the highest-risk group, the small potential benefit does not outweigh the risks of antibiotic use.
rules.source_locator: Conditions for which prophylaxis is not recommended.

recommendation.summary: Amoxicillin 2 g orally, single dose, 30–60 minutes before the procedure.

rules.rationale: Amoxicillin is the standard oral prophylaxis agent for at-risk patients.

recommendation.summary: Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg orally (max 2 g), single dose, 30–60 minutes before the procedure.

rules.rationale: Weight-based amoxicillin, capped at the adult dose.

recommendation.summary: Penicillin allergy without anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria: cephalexin 2 g, OR azithromycin/clarithromycin 500 mg, OR doxycycline 100 mg — single oral dose 30–60 min before.

options.label: Cephalexin (oral)
options.notes: Avoid if any history of anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria to penicillins.

contraindications: cephalosporins if history of anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria to penicillin/ampicillin
rules.rationale: Clindamycin is no longer recommended; cephalexin is an option only when the allergy is not severe.

recommendation.summary: Severe penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria): azithromycin/clarithromycin 500 mg OR doxycycline 100 mg — single oral dose. Do NOT use a cephalosporin.

rules.rationale: With severe penicillin allergy, cephalosporins are avoided; a macrolide or doxycycline is used.

recommendation.summary: Cephalexin 50 mg/kg (if not severe allergy), OR azithromycin/clarithromycin 15 mg/kg, OR doxycycline (<45 kg: 2.2 mg/kg; ≥45 kg: 100 mg) — single oral dose.

rules.rationale: Paediatric penicillin-allergy alternatives, weight-based and capped at adult doses.

recommendation.summary: Unable to take oral medication: ampicillin 2 g IM/IV, OR cefazolin/ceftriaxone 1 g IM/IV — single dose 30–60 min before.

rules.rationale: Parenteral options when oral administration is not possible.
rules.source_locator: Prophylactic regimen table (unable to take oral).

recommendation.summary: Penicillin allergy (non-severe) and unable to take oral: cefazolin or ceftriaxone 1 g IM/IV, single dose. For severe (anaphylactic) allergy, cephalosporins are contraindicated — seek medical/specialist advice.

options.label: Cefazolin or ceftriaxone (IM/IV)
options.notes: Do not use if history of anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria to penicillin/ampicillin.

contraindications: cephalosporins if severe penicillin allergy — obtain specialist advice
rules.rationale: Cephalosporin parenteral option when non-severe allergy; no simple parenteral option for severe allergy since clindamycin is no longer recommended.
rules.source_locator: Prophylactic regimen table (penicillin allergy, unable to take oral).

recommendation.summary: Child unable to take oral medication: ampicillin 50 mg/kg IM/IV, OR cefazolin/ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IM/IV — single dose 30–60 min before.

rules.rationale: Paediatric parenteral options when oral administration is not possible.
rules.source_locator: Prophylactic regimen table (paediatric, unable to take oral).

recommendation.summary: Severe (anaphylactic) penicillin allergy AND unable to take oral medication: there is no simple recommended regimen (cephalosporins are contraindicated and clindamycin is no longer recommended). Obtain medical/specialist advice.

cautions: seek specialist/medical advice for an alternative agent
rules.rationale: AHA 2021 provides no straightforward parenteral option for anaphylactic penicillin allergy after clindamycin was removed.
rules.source_locator: Prophylactic regimen table (penicillin allergy, unable to take oral).

recommendation.summary: In the UK, antibiotic prophylaxis against IE is NOT recommended routinely (NICE CG64). For higher-risk patients needing special consideration, decide on an individualised, shared-decision basis with the patient and cardiologist. If prophylaxis is agreed, SDCEP advises: amoxicillin 3 g oral (single sachet) 60 min before; penicillin-allergic: clindamycin 600 mg. (Note: unlike the US/AHA, UK guidance still lists clindamycin for IE prophylaxis.)

options.label: Clindamycin (penicillin allergy)
options.notes: UK retains clindamycin for IE prophylaxis; weigh C. difficile risk.

options.label: Children (weight-based)
options.notes: Confirm paediatric doses against current SDCEP/BNFc.

cautions: UK position differs from the US — do not apply US routine prophylaxis in a UK setting without checking NICE/SDCEP
shared decision-making; discuss antibiotic harms with the patient
rules.rationale: NICE CG64 advises prophylaxis is not recommended routinely; a 2016 amendment added special-consideration guidance for higher-risk groups. SDCEP implementation advice gives the regimen for when prophylaxis is agreed.
rules.source_locator: NICE CG64; SDCEP Antibiotic Prophylaxis Against IE — Implementation Advice (prescribing advice).
